Maria S.: Heads-up — AcmeCorp (tenant acme) opened a P1: lots of 429s in prod starting ~09:12 UTC after yesterday's billing plan migration. Customer says call volumes are same but bursts get throttled. Sample req ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Ticket: https://support.internal/acme/789. Not sure if noisy neighbor or quota remap. Can someone triage? :eyes:

Cheng L.: I'm on it. Any deploys or infra changes around the migration time?

Maria S.: Deploy-bot shows the billing-migration job finished 2026-03-16T23:50Z. No other infra deploys listed. Customer says they hit 429 on almost every >n requests/s spike. Latency is OK, it's just rejections.

deploy-bot: billing-migration-service finished run id=bm-20260316-2350 status=SUCCESS migrated_tenants=24

Bob D.: Can you paste the tenant's rate profile after migration? pulling now...

Maria S.: Output from internal-api: 

```
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "rate_units": 3600,
  "burst": 200,
  "rate_multiplier": null,
  "unit_denominator": "minutes"
}
```

This looks wrong — rate_units=3600 and unit_denominator=minutes effectively gives them 3600 requests/minute? That seems inverted vs expectation (we expected per-hour units).

Cheng L.: Oof. If unit_denominator is minutes but value is meant for hours, that reduces their effective budget by 60x. That would explain immediate 429s on spikes. Did the migration script change unit_denominator semantics?

Bob D.: Confirming with DB: migration job wrote unit_denominator based on plan.token_window field. Looks like for a subset we defaulted to "minutes" when plan.token_window was null. I'll open quick fix.

Priya K.: Customer on a reserved plan that was supposed to be converted to per-hour units during billing migration. They were charged for the new plan so this is high priority to fix and refund if needed.

Cheng L.: Repro steps I ran from my laptop (non-prod repro, 5s intervals):

```
# repro flood (do not run in prod)
sendload --tenant acme --rps 150 --duration 120s --header "X-Request-ID: repro-01"
# observed ~80% 429s within 30s
```

Observed identical behavior against staging when unit_denominator forced to minutes.

Bob D.: Hotfix applied: updated tenant.rate_profile.unit_denominator -> "hours" for acme and 3 other tenants affected, restarted quota service (rolling). Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/migration-fixes/pull/42 :shipit:

Maria S.: Customer notified about fix and asking for ETA on refunds and whether there will be follow-ups. Thank you.

Priya K.: I'll draft refund + incident note. Ask billing to queue credit for 03/16-03/17 spike window.

Cheng L.: Root cause: billing-migration defaulted null token_window -> minutes. Follow-ups: add migration unit test, disallow null token_window, add a pre-migration dry-run alert that compares before/after effective rate (units * denominator). Also added temporary alert that watches sudden effective-unit drops (>10x) per tenant.

Bob D.: Created infra ticket to add a migration verifier job (links + sample scripts) and scheduled a retro with billing engineering tomorrow.

Maria S.: Customer confirmed 429 rate dropped to near-zero after fix. Closing P1 after billing credits confirmed. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: incident-note created https://incidents.internal/incident/2026-03-acme-throttle-migration

Cheng L.: Marking this resolved but leaving follow-ups in backlog: RB-314 migration tests, RB-315 migration verifier. :eyes:
